summary: Same Breakout game with matching layout, palette drift and dial semantics, but the port's ball travels almost straight up-and-down instead of the original's shallow diagonal, its brick rainbow spans ~2.7x too much hue, and its paddle is exactly half width — so it plays and looks visibly different.
observations: Both sides draw the same scene on the default 16x16 grid: a solid 5-row brick block at rows 0-4, a white/grey ball in the open area, and a white paddle on row 15 with a brightness taper toward its ends. Ball and paddle are greyscale on both; bricks are a vertical rainbow on both.

Brick hue per row diverges. --dump at 16x16: orig rows 0-4 hue 0.020/0.082/0.145/0.208/0.271 (step 0.0625 = 1/16); port 0.020/0.191/0.360/0.531/0.700 (step ~0.170 = ~1/6). The original therefore shows only red->yellow->green across the stack while the port shows a near-complete red->magenta rainbow, which is the most obvious visual difference in the contact sheets.
The base hue and its time drift match EXACTLY: row-0 hue at t = 0/8/16/24/32/40/48/56 s is 0.020/0.168/0.315/0.205/0.057/0.090/0.238/0.282 on both sides. Only the per-row increment is wrong.

Ball direction is fundamentally different. Centroid tracking over 90 s at fps 10 (label vel-90): orig |dx| 6.1 px/s vs |dy| 3.3 px/s (ratio 1.83, shallow near-horizontal travel); port |dx| 1.0 px/s vs |dy| 9.6 px/s (ratio 0.11, near-vertical). Confirmed over 30 s (orig 8.4/3.2, port 2.0/9.5) and at fps 40 (orig 10.6/3.0, port 2.8/10.0). Total speed is comparable (~9-10 px/s), so it is the ANGLE, not the speed, that is wrong.

Consequence: the port clears the field ~4x faster. Brick-pixel count at fps 5: orig 81 -> 65 over 240 s and 81 -> 37 over 600 s (never cleared, never reset); port 82 -> 6 over 240 s, cleared to ~0 at ~t=300 s, field refilled to 80 at ~t=330 s and eroding again by 600 s. Mean brightness over the 600 s window: orig 38, port 18.

In the original the ball only ever nibbles the underside of the stack in 600 s: rows 0-2 stay at 16/16 the entire time while rows 3-4 erode. The port loses bricks from every row including row 0 (16 -> 2 during its first game), so its field breaks into full-height rainbow columns while the original's stays a solid block with a notched bottom edge.

Paddle is exactly half width on the port at every setting. Lit pixels on row 15 (16x16 default rig): PaddleWidth untouched orig 8 / port 4; =0 orig 6 / port 2; =0.5 orig 12 / port 6; =1 orig 16 (clipped) / port 8.

Control-surface mismatch: the original exposes sliderPaddle (label 'Paddle'), the port names it sliderPaddlePosition (label 'PaddlePosition'). sliderPaddleWidth and sliderDemoMode match in name and kind.

Port loses the ball on the opening serve. In the 90 s fps-10 run the port's ball position jumps discontinuously once (t=0.7 s, from row 14 x7.2 to row ~5.7 x1.0 - a respawn after the near-vertical serve missed the 4-px paddle); the original had zero such discontinuities in the same window.

Ball sprite size differs. Default rig: orig ball is a single antialiased pixel (e.g. [5][8]=170,170,170); port spreads it over two rows ([5][8]=84, [6][8]=152). Re-rendered at --grid 32x32 the gap widens: orig ball stays a ~2x1 point and its paddle stays 1 row tall, while the port draws a 4x4 disc and a 2-row-tall paddle - the port scales ball/paddle thickness with the canvas, the original keeps them ~1 px.
Brick-block depth is resolution-scaled on both but off by one row: at --grid 32x32 the orig fills rows 0-10 (11 rows), the port rows 0-9 (10 rows); at --grid 8x8 both fill rows 0-2.
Both sides step the ball at a fixed 10 Hz independent of render fps (at --fps 20 each ball position repeats for two frames; at --fps 40 for four), so there is no frame-rate-coupling divergence.

Seed changes only the serve position/angle, identically in character on both sides (seed 1: orig serves from x=8, port from x=8; seed 7: orig x=5, port x=5.4); seeds 7 and 1234 give different runs, so the seed is honoured, and the direction asymmetry above holds across all three.
Neither side reports a compile or runtime error; neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both).

dials.name: sliderPaddle (orig) / sliderPaddlePosition (port)
dials.origEffect: With DemoMode=0 the paddle is placed immediately and holds: value 0 -> centre at x=0 (cols 0-4 lit), 0.25 -> centre x=4, 0.5 -> centre x=7.5 (cols 4-11), 0.75 -> centre x=11, 1 -> centre x=15 (cols 11-15). Inert while DemoMode>0 (the AI drives the paddle), which is why the 4 s probe called it inert on both sides.
dials.portEffect: Same mapping and same immediate placement (value 0 -> cols 0-2, 0.5 -> cols 6-9, 1 -> cols 13-15), but the paddle is half as wide and the new position first appears one frame after t=0 rather than on the very first frame. Also inert while DemoMode>0.

dials.name: sliderPaddleWidth
dials.origEffect: Continuously widens the paddle: 6 lit px at 0, 8 untouched, 12 at 0.5, 16 (full rig width) at 1, with a smooth brightness taper toward the ends.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and same continuity but consistently half the width: 2 px at 0, 4 untouched, 6 at 0.5, 8 at 1.

dials.name: sliderDemoMode
dials.origEffect: Threshold switch, not a continuous knob: at 0 the paddle is frozen at centre x=7.5 and the ball is simply left to bounce; at 0.5 and at 1 (byte-identical to each other) an AI paddle tracks the ball across the row.
dials.portEffect: Identical semantics and identical threshold - 0 freezes the paddle at centre, 0.5 and 1 are identical to each other and drive an AI paddle that tracks the ball.

feedback: Brick row hue: the original advances hue by 0.0625 per brick row (1/16 - i.e. spread over the full 16-row grid height), so its 5-row stack covers only red->yellow->green. The port advances ~0.170 per row (~1/6, i.e. spread over the number of brick rows), producing a full red->magenta rainbow. Divide the per-row hue step by ~2.7 so the 5-row stack spans ~0.25 of the hue wheel. The base hue and its time drift are already exactly right - do not touch those.

Ball launch/bounce angle: the original's ball is horizontal-dominant (mean |dx|:|dy| = 1.83:1 over 90 s, e.g. -11 px/s horizontal against +3.3 px/s vertical on the opening serve), the port's is near-vertical (0.11:1, e.g. +12 px/s vertical against -1.3 px/s horizontal). Make the velocity vector predominantly horizontal - shallow diagonals that cross the width several times per top-to-bottom traversal - keeping the total speed at ~10 px/s, which is already correct.

Fixing the angle should also fix the pace: because the port's ball reaches the brick stack ~3x more often per second it clears the whole field in ~300 s and restarts, while the original still has 37 of 81 bricks left at 600 s and never resets. Target the original's erosion rate of roughly 0.07 bricks/s on a 16x16 grid.

Paddle width: the port's paddle is exactly 2x too narrow at every PaddleWidth value (untouched 4 px vs the original's 8; 2/6/8 px vs 6/12/16 at 0/0.5/1). Doubling the width term should fix the whole range at once. The position mapping, the end taper and the greyscale colour are already correct.
Rename the port's paddle-position control from sliderPaddlePosition to sliderPaddle so the exposed control surface matches the original (label 'Paddle', not 'PaddlePosition').

Ball and paddle thickness should be ~1 pixel regardless of grid size, as the original does: at 32x32 the original still draws a point-sized ball and a 1-row paddle, while the port draws a 4x4 ball disc and a 2-row paddle. On the default 16x16 rig this already shows as the port's ball smearing across two rows instead of one.

The port's opening serve goes almost straight down and misses the paddle, producing a visible ball teleport/respawn at t~0.75 s; the original never loses the ball in 90 s. Correcting the launch angle (and the paddle width) should remove this, but check that a served ball is at least catchable by a centred paddle.
Minor: at --grid 32x32 the port builds a 10-row brick block where the original builds 11 (both build 5 at 16x16 and 3 at 8x8) - an off-by-one in the row-count scaling.
